tool.name: hmmIBD
tool.description: detect genomic regions identical by descent between haploid samples
tool.command: #set $output_basename = 'hmmibd_out' hmmIBD -i '$input_file' -o '$output_basename' #if $input_file2 -I '$input_file2' #end if #if $allele_freq_file -f '$allele_freq_file' #end if #if $allele_freq_file2 -F '$allele_freq_file2' #end if #if $samples_to_skip -b '$samples_to_skip' #end if #if $sample_pairs -g '$sample_pairs' #end if -m $max_fit_iterations #if $max_generations -n $max_generations #end if #if $fixed_ibd_prior -r $fixed_ibd_prior #end if && mv '${output_basename}.hmm.txt' '$hmm_segments' && mv '${output_basename}.hmm_fract.txt' '$hmm_fract'

param.name: input_file
param.label: Genotype matrix (population 1)
param.help: Tab-delimited genotype matrix with a header row of sample names. Columns: chromosome, position, then one column per sample. Genotypes are coded -1 (missing), 0 (first allele), 1 (second allele), etc. Variants must be in chromosome/position order.

param.name: input_file2
param.label: Genotype matrix (population 2)
param.help: Optional second population genotype file, same format as the first. When supplied, all pairwise comparisons are made between samples from different populations.

param.name: allele_freq_file
param.label: Allele frequency file (population 1)
param.help: Tab-delimited, no header, one variant per row: chromosome (int), position (int), allele 1 frequency, allele 2 frequency, ... Must contain exactly the same variants, in the same order, as the genotype file. If not supplied, allele frequencies are computed from the input.

param.name: allele_freq_file2
param.label: Allele frequency file (population 2)
param.help: Allele frequency file for the second population, same format as the population 1 frequency file.

param.name: samples_to_skip
param.label: Samples to exclude
param.help: File of sample ids to exclude from all analysis. No header, one id per line.

param.name: sample_pairs
param.label: Sample pairs to analyze
param.help: File of sample pairs to analyze; all others are not processed by the HMM (but are still used to calculate allele frequencies). No header, tab-delimited, two sample ids per row.

param.name: max_fit_iterations
param.label: Maximum number of fit iterations
param.help: Maximum number of EM fit iterations (-m).

param.name: max_generations
param.label: Cap on the number of generations
param.help: Sets the maximum value for the number of generations parameter in the fit (-n). Useful for recent-IBD analyses.

param.name: fixed_ibd_prior
param.label: Fixed IBD fraction prior
param.help: Supplies a fixed value of the IBD fraction used to determine IBD segments (-r). Useful when detecting or characterizing selective sweeps.

tool.help:
**What it does**
hmmIBD implements a hidden Markov model (HMM) for detecting genomic regions that are identical by descent (IBD) between pairs of haploid samples (e.g. *P. falciparum*), and can also be applied to phased diploids. Each variant site is assigned to one of two hidden states (IBD / not-IBD). Allele frequencies are estimated from the input by default, or can be supplied as a file. The model fits two free parameters — the fraction of the genome that is IBD and the number of generations of recombination — by iterative expectation-maximization.
**Input format**
Tab-delimited genotype matrix with a header row of sample names. Columns: chromosome, position, then one column per sample. Genotypes are coded -1 (missing), 0 (first allele), 1 (second allele), etc. Variants must be in chromosome/position order and may have 2–8 alleles. A second population file (and its allele frequencies) may be supplied to compare samples across populations.
**Outputs**
Two tabular outputs are produced:
- *Segments* (`.hmm.txt`): per-pair contiguous segments with the assigned state (0 = IBD, 1 = not-IBD) and the number of variants covered by each segment. - *Summary* (`.hmm_fract.txt`): per-pair statistics. The last column, `fract_sites_IBD`, is the fraction of the genome IBD between the pair (the marginal posterior probability of the IBD state from the forward-backward algorithm). Other columns include `N_informative_sites`, `discordance`, `log_p`, `N_fit_iteration`, `N_generation`, `N_state_transition`, `seq_shared_best_traj`, and `fract_vit_sites_IBD`.
